question: The atomic number is defined as the total number of __________ present in the nucleus of an atom.

options.text: neutrons and half of the protons

solution:
The correct answer is __**only protons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **atomic number** of an element is defined as the total number of **protons** present in the nucleus of its atom. This is a fundamental property of an element and remains constant for all atoms of that element.
 
• The atomic number is symbolized by the letter **Z**. For example, for Hydrogen, Z = 1, as it has one proton in its nucleus.
 
• **Neutrons** do not determine the atomic number. Although neutrons are present in the nucleus, their count can vary in isotopes of an element without affecting the atomic number.
 
• The atomic number is used to uniquely identify an element in the periodic table. For example, Carbon has an atomic number of 6, which means it has 6 protons in its nucleus.
 
• Electrons in a neutral atom are equal in number to the protons, but they are not considered in defining the atomic number.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Protons**:

 
 
• Protons are positively charged particles found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The number of protons determines the chemical identity of an element. For instance, Oxygen always has 8 protons.
 
• Each proton has a charge of **+1e** (positive elementary charge) and a mass of approximately 1 atomic mass unit (amu).
 
 
 
• **Neutrons**:
 
 
• Neutrons are neutral particles (no charge) also located in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The number of neutrons can vary among atoms of the same element, leading to the formation of **isotopes**.
 
• For example, Carbon has three common isotopes: Carbon-12 (6 neutrons), Carbon-13 (7 neutrons), and Carbon-14 (8 neutrons).
 
 
 
• **Electrons**:
 
 
• Electrons are negatively charged particles that orbit the nucleus in different energy levels or shells.
 
• In a neutral atom, the number of electrons is equal to the number of protons.
 
• Electrons play a crucial role in chemical bonding and reactions but do not affect the atomic number.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes**:
 
 
• Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
 
• For example, Hydrogen has three isotopes: Protium (1 proton, 0 neutrons), Deuterium (1 proton, 1 neutron), and Tritium (1 proton, 2 neutrons).
 
• Despite having different masses, isotopes of the same element have identical chemical properties.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table**:
 
 
• The periodic table is arranged in order of increasing atomic number (number of protons).
 
• Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties because they have the same number of valence electrons.
 
• For instance, Group 1 elements like Sodium and Potassium have a single valence electron and exhibit similar reactivity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Atomic Mass Number (A):** It is the sum of the number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom. For example, for Carbon-12, A = 6 (protons) + 6 (neutrons) = 12.
 
• **Neutral Atom:** In a neutral atom, the number of protons equals the number of electrons, maintaining electrical neutrality.
 
• **Ions:** When an atom loses or gains electrons, it becomes an ion. For example, Sodium (Na) loses one electron to form Na⁺, and Chlorine (Cl) gains one electron to form Cl⁻.
 
• **Discovery of Protons:** Protons were discovered by **Ernest Rutherford** in 1917 during his gold foil experiment.
